page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the ARM64 architecture, this server features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard computational tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests score 1519.39 and 6055.47 respectively, placing them in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show 72.78 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 35.07 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance demonstrates weaker performance in memory-intensive and complex instruction sets, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 2702.34 and a PassMark memory score of 1046.13.

Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, optimizing it for network-bound workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a resource-dense compute profile with dedicated cores at a lower hardware class tier, though it lacks advanced vector and matrix extensions. This instance is best suited for scale-out workloads, lightweight database operations, static web serving, and basic containerized applications that benefit from dedicated ARM cores and optimized network throughput.
